body.text: Why is Mimar Sinan's Selimiye Mosque a UNESCO masterpiece?

Completed in 1575 for Sultan Selim II, Selimiye Mosque represents chief Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan's self-proclaimed masterwork, uniting a single colossal dome supported by eight massive piers with four soaring minarets and peak-period İznik ceramic tiles into one unified, remarkably light-filled prayer hall.

Inscribed on the [UNESCO World Heritage List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1366/) in 2011, the Selimiye Mosque and its surrounding social complex (külliye)—including madrasas, a covered market (arasta), a clock house, and a library—solved an architectural challenge Sinan pursued for decades: creating an unobstructed single-dome prayer hall rivaling Hagia Sophia's span. Following a major four-year conservation program, [Selimiye Mosque fully reopened in 2026](https://www.dailysabah.com/turkiye/turkiye-reopens-sinans-selimiye-mosque-after-major-restoration/news), allowing visitors to view its restored dome calligraphy, marble minbar, and 16th-century İznik ceramics free of scaffolding.
Can you visit Edirne as a day trip from Istanbul?

Yes—Edirne sits roughly 235 to 245 kilometers west of central Istanbul along the O-3 motorway, making a 2.5-to-3-hour private drive or chauffeur transfer comfortable for a full day trip, though an overnight stay adds calm evening walks along the Meriç River.

Most historic monuments cluster within a compact walkable core, while the Health Museum and Meriç Bridge sit 10 minutes away by car or local taxi. Public buses run frequently from Istanbul's Esenler Otogar in roughly 3.5 to 4 hours, and [TCDD Taşımacılık](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/) runs regional trains from Halkalı to [Edirne Train Station](https://www.edirne.com.tr/en/how-to-go-edirne/railway), though rail takes longer than driving.

body.text: What else is worth seeing (Old Mosque, Health Museum, Meriç Bridge)?

Beyond Selimiye, Edirne's standout heritage stops are the 15th-century Old Mosque (Eski Cami) for its monumental wall calligraphy, the Sultan Bayezid II Health Museum for Ottoman music therapy history, and the 12-arch stone Meriç Bridge leading directly into leafy Karaağaç along the river.
Structure your sightseeing loop in this order to avoid backtracking:

items: Old Mosque (Eski Cami): Built between 1403 and 1414, [Edirne's oldest surviving imperial mosque](https://turkisharchaeonews.net/object/old-mosque-edirne) features nine domes and oversized black calligraphic inscriptions painted directly across its piers and walls.
Üç Şerefeli Mosque & Covered Bazaars: A five-minute walk west, inspect the 1447 mosque's four distinct minaret patterns and browse the restored Ali Paşa Bazaar.

Complex of Sultan Bayezid II Health Museum: Operated by [Trakya University](https://saglikmuzesi-en.trakya.edu.tr/pages/history), this 1488 darüşşifa (hospital) along the Tunca River demonstrates how Ottoman physicians treated patients using acoustics, classical makam music, water fountains, and herbal remedies.

Meriç Bridge (Mecidiye Köprüsü): Completed in 1847 across the Meriç River, this [263-meter stone bridge](https://www.edirne.com.tr/en/place/meric-bridge/50) with 12 pointed arches and a central marble viewing pavilion is Edirne's finest sunset vantage point.

body.text: What local dishes (tava ciğer, badem ezmesi) define Edirne?

Edirne's Thracian table is defined by tava ciğer—paper-thin beef liver floured and flash-fried in hot sunflower oil—paired with crisp dried red chilies, brined Edirne white cheese, and Ottoman palace almond sweets led by badem ezmesi and Kavala kurabiyesi.

Unlike the spice-heavy kitchens of southeastern Türkiye, [Edirne's culinary tradition](https://tggourmet.com/blogs/tg-gourmet/edirne-food-guide-tava-cigeri-badem-ezmesi) relies on clean, direct flavors shaped by Thracian dairy and Balkan trade. Order tava ciğer at a dedicated lunch house near the Old Mosque, where cooks fry each portion to order in seconds so the exterior crisps while the interior stays tender. Afterward, stop at a historic confectioner for [badem ezmesi](https://edirne.gov.tr/badem-ezmesi)—a smooth paste of blanched almonds, sugar, and water inherited from the Ottoman palace kitchens—alongside crumbly almond-butter Kavala kurabiyesi and aged Edirne beyaz peynir (white cheese).

faq.q: Is the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne open to visitors in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. Following a comprehensive four-year restoration, the UNESCO-listed Selimiye Mosque reopened for worship in February 2026 and fully reopened to visitors in June 2026.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Istanbul to Edirne?
faq.a: Driving from central Istanbul to Edirne along the O-3 (TEM) motorway takes approximately 2.5 to 3 hours depending on Istanbul exit traffic, covering about 235 to 245 kilometers.

faq.q: Is Edirne worth an overnight stay instead of a day trip?
faq.a: While you can cover Selimiye Mosque, the Old Mosque, the Health Museum, and lunch in a well-paced day trip, staying one night lets you walk Meriç Bridge at sunset and dine unhurriedly in Karaağaç.

faq.q: What makes the Sultan Bayezid II Health Museum famous?
faq.a: Built in 1488, the hospital (darüşşifa) treated mental and physical illnesses using water sounds, music therapy, and medicinal scents, and is now an award-winning museum operated by Trakya University.

faq.q: What is Edirne tava ciğer served with?
faq.a: Thinly sliced, floured, and flash-fried beef liver is served hot with crispy dried red Karaağaç chilies, raw sliced onions, tomatoes, and fresh bread—never heavy sauces.

faq.q: Can I take a train from Istanbul to Edirne?
faq.a: Yes, TCDD Taşımacılık operates regional rail services from Istanbul's Halkalı station to Edirne, though driving or booking a private transfer is significantly faster for a single-day itinerary.
